grammar_notes: Fronting of negative/limiting adverbials; fronting of place and movement adverbials; inversion with noun subjects and ordinary order with pronoun subjects.
priming: An ancestor may leave a relic that connects us to our heritage.
Genealogy helps us explore ancestry without reducing identity to ethnicity.
A feast can reinvigorate a tradition, and its significance may become a beacon for younger generations.
Adoptive families also build shared traditions, even when disagreements cause friction.
writing_prompt: Write an essay of about 250 words: Our roots influence us, but they do not define us. To what extent do you agree? Discuss the roles of upbringing, inherited background and personal choice. Consider a contrasting perspective and reach a reasoned conclusion. You may use general or invented examples; personal family disclosure is not required. Do not copy task sentences or the reading preview.

oral_individual: Would you want to take a DNA ancestry test? Explain the possible benefits and concerns.
Which shapes identity more strongly: upbringing or genes? Support your view.
When can a family tradition provide connection, and when can it create pressure?
What makes a place significant to a person or a community? You may use an invented example.
Should endangered languages be actively preserved? Explain your reasoning.
Do family ties create stronger obligations than friendships? Explain and qualify your view.
oral_dialogue: A community is planning a cultural celebration for younger residents. Student A wants to preserve familiar rituals; Student B wants a more inclusive modern format. Agree on two activities and explain how they respect the heritage.

A university is considering offering DNA ancestry tests to students. Student A argues for the educational benefits; Student B raises privacy and interpretation concerns. Agree on safeguards and decide whether the project should go ahead.
A town has a small cultural budget. Student A wants to support an endangered local language; Student B wants to support a widely attended annual celebration. Negotiate an allocation and justify it.

A family disagrees about attendance at its annual celebration. Student A values shared obligations; Student B values individual boundaries. Agree on a compromise that preserves relationships without requiring anyone to disclose private experiences.
